Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is an AI-piloted fork of OrcaSlicer. Its managed autosave saves projects under the app data folder (`jusprin/projects/<id>/`) with a version history. While testing the new JusPrin Preferences window's restart-on-language-change (branch `claude/musing-wing-e808a9`), a session made the project folder unwritable to force a refused restart. The restart was refused correctly, but if the folder stays unwritable, the version store eventually throws an uncaught "cannot open ...manifest.json" error and the app crashes. That is an existing bug, independent of Preferences. Kenneth wants such issues resolved by sessions, not left to him, and prefers plain-English reports.

Task:
Fix a crash in JusPrin's managed autosave and version history. When a project's folder becomes unwritable, autosave retries every 2 seconds. About 20 seconds later the version store throws an uncaught error, "cannot open ...versions\...\manifest.json", and JusPrin crashes. This happens without any special action; the Preferences session found it while testing a refused restart by making the project folder unwritable.

Where to look: the autosave and version store under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/` (for example `ProjectAutosave`), and `agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md` for the intended failure behaviour.

Follow AGENTS.md "Error handling discipline". Don't just swallow the exception. Find which layer should own an unwritable folder as an expected state (a failed save is already a visible state: "Changes couldn't be saved. JusPrin will retry."). Make that path recover visibly, and keep unexpected errors visible.

Done means:
- reproduce the crash on `jusprin-newui` in your own worktree and build tree under C:\b, with your own WebView2 user-data folder;
- fix it in JusPrin's own files;
- add a test that covers the unwritable-folder transition;
- confirm in the running app that JusPrin stays up and recovers once the folder is writable again;
- commit to your branch and report.

The C: drive has only about 2 GB free, so keep build output lean and don't copy build trees. Don't push.

description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1e908987-3ebc-4e47-9372-ca2af82d4fee

---

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).

- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.

**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.

**Concurrent harness runs collide on WebView2 (2026-09-25):** every harness exe uses the same WebView2
profile, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. While another session's harness is running (e.g. a
long `--home-printers-live` fixture run), a second harness fails at once with
`shell_agent_page_handshake_complete FAIL`, and its app log shows `JusPrin agent page failed to load:
The group or resource is not in the correct state`. That is not a page or bundle problem. Check for
`shell_integration_harness.exe` in `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, don't kill another session's
process, and set `$env:WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER='C:\b\<tree>-webview'` for your own runs.

**Scripting on this box (2026-10-06; Python corrected 2026-10-21):** no `python`/`py` on PATH, but Python 3.13 is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\python-3.13.9\python.exe` and runs the prompt suites (`tests/project_prompt`, set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`). Otherwise use node (`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). Bash heredocs and `node -e "..."` that contain backticks, `${...}` or backslashes get mangled by the shell; write the script to a file with the Write tool and run `node <file>`. The main checkout's build tree `C:\src\JusPrin\build` (VS generator, Release) is fine to build from a session that is working in the main checkout: `cmake --build C:\src\JusPrin\build --config Release --target <targets> -- -m` after `vcvars64.bat`; harness exes there read `resources\` from the source tree, so `npm run build` in `AgentUI` is enough to refresh the Agent page. A touched `Workspace.hpp` rebuild of `libslic3r_gui` + `shell_integration_harness` takes roughly 10 minutes.

name: native-ui-synthetic-input-and-capture
description: "Driving JusPrin's native (wx) UI on the Windows box with real pointer and key input from PowerShell, and capturing it — the four traps that each looked like an app bug"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5f4606f5-f6a6-45fd-a91f-ea049831eb87
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:59.148Z
---

With the RDP session **connected** (see [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]] for the disconnected case), native wx surfaces can be driven from PowerShell with `SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` + `keybd_event` and captured with `Graphics.CopyFromScreen`. Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:

- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).

**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].

**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.

Related harness facts from the same session:
- `workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe` gets no runtime DLLs copied beside it; run it with `C:\b\<tree>\tests\shell\Release` on `PATH` or it exits `0xC0000135`.
- In the default shell-harness mode, `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release` and `earlier_model_version_available` fail on Windows on an unmodified build too: the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores. Since the Check Print crash was fixed (2026-10-14, `20de313d92`) the default mode runs to the end on this box: 552 pass, 6 fail. The other two failures, `agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client_shrinking_to_1000_dip` and `growing_to_1400_dip`, also fail with the fix switched off, with identical geometry, so they predate it. The filament-menu keyboard checks (`down_selects_the_first_filament` etc.) failed in 1 of 4 runs of the same binary, and that run then stalled on an open setup guide. See [[windows-build-machine]].
- A baseline for "is this failure mine": copy `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\*` to a scratch dir and run that exe (copying avoids locking the shared build's exe).

name: crash-stacks-without-a-debugger
description: "Get a symbolized call stack for a native crash on the Windows box in minutes: C:\\b\\minidbg (Win32 debug API) plus a build tree compiled with /Z7 and linked /DEBUG; traps that cost a full rebuild"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c04fbdd1-d707-42dc-922c-7911bb1d35e0
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:52.100Z
---

`C:\b\minidbg\minidbg.exe <exe> [args]` (source `minidbg.cpp` beside it, built with `cl /std:c++17 /EHsc /DUNICODE`) runs a program under the Win32 debug API and prints a symbolized stack, with file:line where a PDB exists, for every access violation, heap corruption, stack-buffer overrun and second-chance exception. No WinDbg download needed. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1`. `run-harness-example.ps1` there shows the env setup for the shell harness. Used 2026-10-14 to find the Check Print crash: the stack led straight to `GCodeViewer::init` → `strlen(glGetString(GL_VERSION))` with no current GL context.

For line numbers you need a tree with debug info. Configure with
`"-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=/MD /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /Z7"`, the same for C, and `"-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE=/DEBUG:FULL /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"` (example: `C:\b\ckp-build.cmd`). **Keep `/MD`.** Overriding the flags without it compiles everything `/MT`, and the link fails only at the very end with `LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary mismatch` against opencv/libcurl, after a 40-minute build. `SLIC3R_MSVC_PDB` is declared in CMakeLists.txt but nothing reads it.

Quick triage without any of this: the event-log fault offset in a system DLL maps to a function via `dumpbin /exports <dll>` (the nearest export at or below the offset). ucrtbase `0x2a341` is `strlen+0x31`, meaning a null or bad `char*`.

Run harnesses with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError` rather than PowerShell `2>`. A PowerShell native-command redirect writes the file only when the process exits, so a hung run shows a 0-byte log. Visible windows of a stuck process can be listed with `C:\b\ckp-windows.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (a `#32770` titled 引导_P21 is OrcaSlicer's setup guide left open).

Windows GL fact found the same day: `wxGLCanvas::Create` on MSW always ends with `wglMakeCurrent(nullptr, nullptr)`. Creating any GL canvas leaves no context current, so GL work right after constructing a canvas needs an explicit make-current first. Upstream's helper for this is `GLCanvas3D::_set_shown_canvas_current`.

See [[windows-build-machine]].

result.output:
# Local autosave and version history

JusPrin saves authored projects in the application data directory under
`jusprin/projects/<project-id>/`. The project ID is independent of the source
filename. Opening an external 3MF or model imports it into a managed draft;
autosave never overwrites the source. **Saved** means the printable
project checkpoint and the current JusPrin document are durable. A 3MF is written
to a user-selected path only through **Export project 3MF…**. A copied 3MF does
not include local versions, conversations, or attachments.

The project header's actions menu exposes the save state, version history,
recent local projects, and export. Version history restores an earlier model
and its effective project settings. The native window title shows the managed
project name and the same save state as the header. Orca's dirty asterisk
does not represent whether the local project has been saved. Before restoring,
JusPrin saves and pins
the current version, then records the restore as a new version, so the prior
state remains available. Each older timestamp has a separate Restore button;
clicking the timestamp does nothing, and Restore asks for confirmation. A blank authored project gets one empty baseline
version so it can be reopened; later document edits do not add versions. A
first Agent model operation pins that baseline as its before-version.
Conversations with each chat's intent and plan, audit, and completed print
records remain in the current document; restoring a model marks the active
chat's plan for reassessment. Region descriptions follow the model: each
version records the list it was saved with, and restoring it brings that list
back. Restoring a model does not undo physical prints or change
global printer facts. Agent
mutations save and pin their actual
before-state, then link an after-version and outcome in an operation record.

## Storage and recovery contract

The restoration rules above describe ordinary Version history. **Restore and
resume** is a separate chat transition. Each chat owns its print intent and
plan; the project's current ones are the active chat's. A chat's checkpoint
holds a model-version reference and a structured setup summary of the moment
it was left. Browsing an older chat does not change the working project.
Resuming it saves and pins the outgoing state, restores the model with its
region descriptions, and activates that chat, whose intent and plan never left
it, only after the new document is durable. Other conversations, audit and print
records, and global printer facts remain. This does not add a full project-
document copy to model versions or make document edits create model versions.
Ordinary Version history remains model-only and does not activate an older
chat. An interrupted chat transition leaves a durable pending marker and
blocks that managed project for explicit recovery on restart.

Each model version has Orca backup-format metadata and a manifest of object
resources. It has no copy of the project document. Unchanged object resources are referenced rather
than serialized again. Changed objects are serialized with Orca's split-model
writer into immutable ZIP resources. A renamed object can reuse its resource;
materialization relabels its entry for Orca's native restore loader. Metadata
and each resource are checked for required entries and geometry. The live
Orca backup directory and an imported source file are never version-store
dependencies.

All project records advance one `current-state.json` document without creating
a model version. The document is atomically replaced after 1.5 seconds without
a change, or within 15 seconds during a continuous stream. Agent and project
boundaries wait for the write. Attachments are written once before their
document references become durable; operation records linking before/after
versions are committed once at the operation boundary. A model checkpoint
ensures the current document is durable before it publishes a new `HEAD`.

## Save classification

The autosave controller observes two independent kinds of change. Native
geometry, transforms, paint, plates, and effective project settings can change
what an earlier printable project reconstructs and therefore create a model
version. A change to the region descriptions makes one too, since a version
records them. Document changes, including streamed Agent messages, drafts,
intent, plans, audit records, and print facts, update only the current
document. `docRevision` is a signal to coalesce that write; neither
it nor document contents participate in model-version equality. A workspace
event can prompt a model check, but cannot make unchanged checkpoint content
into a new version.

A project's directory and its lock are created by its first write, so a
blank project nothing was saved for leaves no directory behind. That first
write fails if another instance saved the same project identity in the
meantime. A single writer owns each project through an OS file lock. It writes and
flushes the current document and changed resources before publishing a version directory,
then atomically replaces `HEAD` with the ordered committed-version index.
POSIX also synchronizes containing directories; Windows flushes individual
files and uses `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH`. Restart discards
unfinished staging, unindexed versions, unreachable resources, and old
disposable restore directories. If saving
fails, the current model stays open, the header reports a local save failure,
and the next save retries it. Project replacement is blocked until the live
state is saved. Explicit export validates a temporary 3MF before replacing
its destination.

Older projects may still contain `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json`. On first adoption, JusPrin reads that state and copies its
attachments to the managed store; it does not delete the old source. Once a
managed version exists, local state is authoritative. Reopening a copied
external 3MF with an already managed identity forks a new project identity.
When a file opened as a project matches a saved project, JusPrin asks whether
to create another project or open the existing one directly. A project
remembers the file it was opened from (`openedFrom`) and that file's MD5 then
(`openedDigest`) in each version manifest: a .3mf from its project path, a model
file the agent's `project_open` opened as a new project from the path it gave.
Every way a person opens a .3mf asks, because the check sits in
`Plater::load_project` (File > Open Project, recent files, Finder, drops); the
agent's `project_open` returns the question as `opened_before` and takes the
answer as `openedBefore`. A file whose MD5 differs is a likely new export, so
the question says so and defaults to a new project; otherwise it defaults to
the saved one. Importing a file into a project never asks. If several
projects match, it continues the current one when it came from that file;
otherwise it opens the most recently updated match.
The project document has one schema version and no migration (the project is
not live yet): a document of any other version, like a corrupt one, is
replaced by a fresh document. The local store reads only its current index,
manifest and current-document formats.
Recent projects appear on Home and in the header menu. Selecting one
opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.
The most recently authored local project resumes on startup.

- The controller checks a lightweight native state signature every 2 seconds
  and waits 1.5 seconds after an observed model edit before starting a background
  model save. Document changes use the coalesced state write described above;
  they never call Orca's 3MF exporter. An unchanged project does not run the
  exporter. Project replacement and Agent boundaries save synchronously.
- While the JusPrin shell owns managed autosave, Orca's automatic backup timer
  and object-mesh backup cache are suspended. The configured backup interval is
  left intact and resumes if the shell is detached. Manual 3MF export remains
  available.
- Retention aims for at most 200 versions and 4 GiB per project. These are
  soft limits: the current version, pinned versions, and Agent operation
  references survive even when they exceed the budget. Unreferenced object
  resources and attachments are removed after the retained index is durable.
- A support, seam, color, or fuzzy paint edit can serialize the whole painted
  object because Orca stores triangle paint with its mesh. The coherence
  spike measured about 31 MB and 6.7 seconds of worker time for a large paint
  edit; this is a fixture measurement, not a latency guarantee.
- History is local to this application data directory. There is no portable
  history export or automatic cloud synchronization.

## Verification

The native workspace harness checks the current document across historical
model restores, selective resources, all four paint
channels, empty restore, corrupt and missing resource rejection, export
replacement, locks, retention, and attachment reachability. The shell harness
checks streamed replies without per-word model exports, legacy adoption,
failed-save behavior, restore, restart, and Agent
boundaries. Separate process tests stop publication after resources, version,
and `HEAD`, then verify recovery in a fresh process. These checks run on macOS;
Windows and Linux runtime behavior still needs platform verification before
those builds are released.

Every time the Agent page refreshes, JusPrin builds its list of restore points by re-reading every saved version's `manifest.json` from disk. That read throws, nothing catches it, and the app goes down. The Preferences session's log shows exactly this: 2-second save retries failing, then "Uncaught exception: cannot open …\versions\…\manifest.json".

So the store will read the version list once when the project opens and keep it in memory. Saving adds to that list and cleanup trims it. Screens built from the list then can't fail just because the folder became unreadable; saves still fail visibly and retry. Separately, the "pin this version" step in `pin_current` writes to the folder but could throw past its callers. It will report a failed save instead, which is how its callers already expect failure to look.
- **Test:** a new shell-harness mode, `--unavailable-storage`. It takes away access to the open project's folder (through the folder's access list on Windows, since POSIX permission bits aren't enforced there). ---
name: icacls-write-deny-blocks-reads
description: On Windows, `icacls /deny user:(W)` also blocks opening files for reading; use it (or the shell harness's UnavailableFolder) knowingly when faking an unwritable folder
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`icacls <dir> /deny "guitest:(OI)(CI)(W,D,DC)"` makes the folder **unreadable as well as unwritable**: icacls' "W" includes SYNCHRONIZE, and every normal file open (GENERIC_READ) asks for SYNCHRONIZE. Listing rights explicitly (WD,AD,WEA,WA) gets normalized back to W, so a read-only-but-unwritable folder can't be made this way. Verified 2026-10-23.

POSIX `std::filesystem::permissions` is ignored on Windows, which is why the shell harness's older `failed_autosave_*` checks fail there. The `--unavailable-storage` harness mode (commit fe6175df41, branch claude/autosave-unwritable) has an `UnavailableFolder` RAII helper: an ACL deny on Windows, chmod 000 elsewhere. Reuse it for any "storage went away" test.

Remove a deny with `icacls <dir> /remove:d guitest`. The owner keeps WRITE_DAC, so this works while the deny is in place.

I've fixed the crash and committed it to `claude/autosave-unwritable` as `fe6175df41` (not pushed). Before the fix JusPrin died 10 seconds after its project folder became unusable; with the fix it stays up, shows "Couldn't save", and goes back to "Saved" by itself once the folder is usable again.

**Why it crashed.** The Preferences test blocked "write" on the projects folder. On Windows that also blocks reading files. Every time the Agent page refreshes, it rebuilds its list of restore points by re-reading every saved version's file from disk. That read failed, nothing handled it, and the app went down. It needed no action from the user; just waiting was enough. The saves failing and retrying every 2 seconds was already handled correctly.

**What I changed:**
- **The version list is kept in memory.** A saved version never changes, and only the open project's store writes to it. So the list is now read once when the project opens, then grows on each save and shrinks when old versions are cleaned up. The page no longer touches the disk to show it. Saves into the folder still fail, and the header still says "Couldn't save" and retries.
- **The pin step reports failure the normal way.** When a chat checkpoint marks ("pins") the current version, a write failure there could also escape and crash. It now counts as a failed save, which is the form its callers already handle.
- Unexpected errors still surface as before; I didn't wrap anything broadly.

**Test.** A new shell-harness mode, `--unavailable-storage`, makes the open project's folder unreadable and unwritable. On Windows it does this through the folder's access list, because the POSIX permission bits older tests use are ignored there. It then checks:
- a checkpoint and an edit are refused, with the failure shown;
- the Agent page and version list keep working through several retries;
- saving resumes on its own once access is back.

The unfixed build fails it with the original error; the fixed build passes all 13 checks.

input.content:
Say so on Home when the projects folder can't be read, and keep trying

Opening Home with an unreadable projects folder ended in an uncaught
"directory_iterator: Access is denied" from ProjectAutosave::projects().
Home lists projects by iterating that folder.

- OrcaHomeBackend::recent_projects() is where storage becomes page state.
  It turns a filesystem error from that listing into a ProjectList
  problem. The page shows "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will
  keep trying." instead of "No projects yet." projects() itself stays
  strict; the header's Recent projects menu already shows its errors in a
  dialog.
- While the page shows that problem, HomeHost's once-a-second live refresh
  re-reads the projects. The gallery fills in by itself once the folder is
  readable; Home has no back button to "open it again".
- projects() and projects_for_source() checked each project's HEAD
  outside their per-project error handling. On POSIX, exists() throws for
  a folder without permission, so one locked project could fail the
  whole list. The check is now inside, and that project is left out like
  any other unavailable one.

The --unavailable-storage harness mode now also locks the whole projects
folder with Home open. It checks the page says so and refills by itself
once access returns, and that Home leaves out a single unreadable
project. New jusprin_tests cases cover the payload field and the retry.

Also fixes home_describes_managed_project. It looked for
"/jusprin/projects/" in the project path, which is native and uses
backslashes on Windows; it is only the card's tooltip. The check now
compares the actual folder.

A small test program running the same two calls Home's listing makes showed the folder check still succeeds but reading the folder's contents fails with "Access is denied". Nothing caught that, so opening Home in that state would have taken the app down.
- **Fix:** the Home backend is where saved projects get turned into what the page shows. Only there, a failure to read the projects folder becomes a message on the page: "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying." It replaces the misleading "No projects yet." The lower-level listing still fails loudly; the header's Recent projects menu already shows those errors in a dialog.
- **Retry:** while the message is up, Home re-reads the folder on its existing once-a-second refresh. Home has no back button, so waiting for "next time Home opens" would have left the person stuck on the message.
- **One unreadable project:** a single project folder that can't be read is now left out of the list, like a damaged project already was. Before, the per-project check sat outside that handling. On Windows that check doesn't throw. On macOS/Linux, by the language standard, it throws for a folder with no permissions and would sink the whole list. I couldn't verify that on a Mac.

Stop an open, and say why, when the saved projects can't be read

Opening a file asks whether it was opened before by listing the projects
folder. With that folder unreadable, the Agent's project_open crashed
JusPrin with an uncaught "directory_iterator: Access is denied"
(reproduced in the app). A person's File > Open goes through the same
lookup.

The listing now reports an unreadable projects folder as a result, not
an exception. One helper lists the project folders with the error_code
forms. projects() and projects_for_source() return nothing in that case,
meaning "unknown", which is not the same as "no projects" or "not opened
before". Each caller decides what that means:

- Opening a file stops before anything is replaced, because the
  question can't be answered and a project made from the file couldn't
  be saved either. A person sees "Your saved projects couldn't be read
  ... The file wasn't opened." The Agent's project_open fails with
  local_save_failed (the listed code whose next step, tell the person,
  fits), whether at the request or at its run. ToolExecutionCoordinator's
  lookup callback gains an EarlierLookup with an unreadable flag; a
  callback returning just the optional project still converts to it.
- Home says the projects couldn't be loaded, as before, now without the
  catch added for it.
- The header's Recent projects menu says "Projects couldn't be loaded".

--unavailable-storage checks both opens with the projects folder locked:
nothing opens, the reason is given, and the current project stays. A
coordinator unit test covers the unreadable answer at request and at
run.
